A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rotary Position Encodings for Graphs and the WIRE method. Text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: V3 reports original synthetic graph prediction, point-cloud classification and segmentation, and graph-benchmark experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds spectral-coordinate dimensionality results on four graph benchmarks in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, spectral-coordinate rotations, Performer integration, and the RWPE variant are unchanged. The added dimensionality sweep evaluates an existing method parameter.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic tasks, ModelNet40 and ShapeNet point-cloud tasks, and graph benchmarks. The new ablation uses existing MNIST, CIFAR10, PATTERN, and CLUSTER coverage without changing task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same no-WIRE controls, Cartesian RoPE, Performer, softmax, SGFormer, and BigBird baselines. The additional expander-propagation citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.6 adds a sweep over m = 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 on four retained graph benchmarks. Previously reported splits, metrics, training budgets, and experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 already examines spectral dimensionality on synthetic tasks. V4 extends this sensitivity analysis to four graph benchmarks in Table 10, testing whether intermediate dimensionalities remain preferable. Existing attention-pattern and variant analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The synthetic four-run standard errors, single-seed point-cloud reporting, and benchmark seed counts are unchanged. Table 10 extends the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; Table 3's new highlighting introduces no stated statistical test.

E6.justification: V4 adds dimensionality-sweep results, including CLUSTER accuracies of 77.714 ± 0.064 at m = 8 and 76.848 ± 0.047 at m = 32. These are additional experimental settings. All previously reported table values and figure results are retained, including v3 Tables 10–11 as v4 Tables 11–12.

T1.justification: Lemma 1's proof now explicitly writes L → PLPᵀ and eigenvectors Pu_k, restating the earlier permutation argument. Its qualifications, the grid-recovery and effective-resistance theorems, and the appendix mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, core contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about graph rotary encodings, grid recovery, asymptotic effective-resistance dependence, empirical utility, and compatibility with linear attention.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly explains that RWPE produces less attention modulation between nodes with similar local environments, even when distant. Appendix A.6 interprets intermediate dimensionalities as balancing structural information and inductive bias, and suggests investigating homophily and heterophily.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes the code access pointer from an anonymous WIRE_Graphs archive to the named Graph-RoPE GitHub repository. Existing implementation, hardware, and training-hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds Deac et al. (2022), Expander Graph Propagation, and Wilson et al. (2025), Cayley Graph Propagation, to the existing discussion of expander-based future work. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: V4 adds acknowledgements and author contributions, inserts Appendix A.6, clarifies the permutation-proof wording, and corrects several typos and broken references. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds Table 10, highlights selected WIRE scores in red in Table 3 with an explanatory caption, and corrects the RWPE coordinate heading. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and reflowed; all four figures and the basic document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: New Table 10 extends dimensionality sensitivity evidence from synthetic tasks to four established graph benchmarks, helping readers assess the choice of m. The added RWPE explanation and corrected wording and labels improve clarity. These are useful, limited gains while the method, principal results, and theoretical scope remain stable.
